caption:
PART 2/2 — 53 minutes after the first hit, Nordbay struck New Orleans again. ⚠️🚢

Damaged and still moving, the empty Aframax had to round Algiers Point. Tugs were turned away, the master was on the phone — and at 23:06 she hit the Mandeville Street Wharf. Total damage: about $6.4 million.

NTSB lessons: a pilot on board never removes the master's duty to navigate safely, and no call is more important than a ship still under way.

What would you have done? 👇

Source: NTSB Marine Accident Brief MAB-17/30 (public report). Photos: NTSB report (credits on screen). Animated illustration, not a reconstruction.

#marineaccident #shipping #tanker #neworleans #mississippiriver #seafarer #merchantnavy #bridgeteam #NTSB #maritimesafety #jaimarineshorts

scenes.narration: The master is on the phone. The pilot is shouting for power. And a wounded tanker is heading straight for a wharf.
scenes.direction: Fast and tense, like breaking news.

scenes.headline: [Previously...]
scenes.narration: Previously... an empty tanker, a river in flood, and a dock smashed at Nine-Mile Point. Nordbay is wounded... but she is still moving.
scenes.direction: Quiet, ominous. Pause before 'but she is still moving'.

scenes.headline: Plan: [anchor] below Algiers Point.
scenes.narration: Twenty-two eighteen. The pilot calls for tugs. The decision: keep going, and anchor below Algiers Point, a sharp bend right in the heart of the city.

p.text: Two tugs offer their lines. The pilot [declines.]
p.by: At this speed, he fears dragging them

scenes.narration: Twenty-two thirty-seven. Two tugs come alongside. They offer their lines... and the pilot says no. At this speed, he fears dragging them.
scenes.direction: Slow down on 'and the pilot says no'.

scenes.headline: [22:58] Full ahead.
scenes.sub: Next: hard starboard around Algiers Point
scenes.narration: Twenty-two fifty-eight. Under the Crescent City Connection. Full ahead. Now... one more bend. Hard starboard, around Algiers Point.

scenes.headline: And the master? [On the phone.]
scenes.narration: And the master? Right now... he is on the phone with the shipping company.

p.text: Emergency... [as much as you can give me!]

scenes.narration: Twenty-three oh four. The pilot cries out. Emergency! As much as you can give me! The master drops the call. Full sea speed!

scenes.headline: [Too late.]
scenes.sub: Rate of turn falling · danger signal
scenes.narration: Too late. Her turn is slowing. The bank is rushing closer. Twenty-three oh five. Danger signal. Again.
scenes.direction: Short, breathless lines. Drop low on 'Again.'

scenes.headline: [23:06] Second allision.
scenes.sub: Two hits · one night · 53 minutes apart
scenes.narration: Twenty-three oh six. Impact! Nordbay slams into the Mandeville Street Wharf. Two hits. One night. Fifty-three minutes apart.
scenes.direction: Loud on 'Impact!', then slow and heavy on the last three lines.

scenes.headline: The bill: [$6.4 million].
scenes.narration: The bill? About six point four million dollars. Five propeller blades damaged. Steel buckled in her stern.

scenes.headline: What the [NTSB] found.

items: Risks of handling an empty ship in high water not properly assessed
Strong current behind her, turning into the wind
Bridge team lost track of the ship's position
2nd hit: master distracted by a phone call

scenes.narration: So what really went wrong? The NTSB found the pilot and the master never properly assessed the risk: an empty ship, in high water, with the current behind her, turning into the wind. The bridge team lost track of where the ship was. And the second hit? The master was distracted... by a phone call.
scenes.direction: Investigator voice. Pause before 'by a phone call'.

scenes.headline: [Lessons] for every bridge.

items: A pilot on board never removes the master's duty
After an accident, no call matters more than a ship still moving
Talk through wind, current and ballast condition before the bend

scenes.narration: Lesson one. A pilot on board never takes away the master's duty. Lesson two. After an accident, no phone call matters more than a ship that is still moving. Lesson three. Talk through the wind, the current and your ship's condition before the bend... not in it.
scenes.direction: Firm, like a senior Chief teaching juniors.

scenes.narration: Now tell me... what would you have done on that bridge? Comment below. And follow Jai Marine Shorts for the next case file.
